newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY POLICE REVAMP TO BEAR FRUIT SOON - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY POLICE REVAMP TO BEAR FRUIT SOON - MINISTER.

text.p: Top-level replacements in Hungary's police force, triggered by police's failure to halt a Budapest gangland war, should bear fruit soon, Minister of Interior Gabor Kuncze said on Friday.
"The new national police chief is trusted to be able to produce changes in a very short time," Kuncze told a news conference after announcing the sackings.
He said prime minister Gyula Horn and him had decided to replace national police chief General Sandor Pinter and Budapest police chief General Janos Bodracska.
County police chief Laszlo Forgacs was named as Pinter's successor, pending parliament's approval.
One of Pinter's deputies, Andras Turos and a national police directorate head, Laszlo Valenta had also been sacked.
Kuncze added that the reasons for the sackings were threefold, "the recent series of Budapest events" being one of them.
Since September, Budapest citizens have been rattled by eleven bombings and five armed attacks against people who are believed to have become involved in a war of organised gangs.
One man was killed in the shootings and two more severely injured. The grenade attacks have not injured anyone but have caused serious damage.
The latest incident came on Friday morning when an unknown attacker first shot at a 52-year-old Budapest casino owner and then struck him with his gun before fleeing.
"The recent spate of events has brought to surface many problems (within the police)," Kuncze said, mentioning inefficient handling of finances, corruption and lack of discipline.
"Police needs to be cleansed," he said, adding that "there will be no witchhunt" following Friday's replacements.
However, dozens of high-ranking police officers might choose to quit the force following Friday's reshuffle, a source that wished to remain unnamed told Reuters.
Kuncze said he was not considering resignation, but acknowledged his responsibility concerning public safety.
"If these steps (to restructure the police) do not bring the necessary and expected results, my responsibility could also be considered," he said.
